primary.title: Protective helmets for motorcycle riders - Specification (Third Revision)
primary.summary: IS 4151 specifies construction, materials, field of vision, shock absorption, penetration resistance, retention system strength and effectiveness, rigidity, chin-bar and visor requirements for protective helmets for riders and pillion riders of two-wheeled motor vehicles. All helmets manufactured or sold in India for two-wheeler use must conform to IS 4151 and carry the ISI mark.

sources.doc: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective helmets for motorcycle riders
BIS Product Manual for IS 4151 (June 2020, revised)

related.title: Amendments to IS 4151 : 2015
related.relation: Amendments tighten mass limits and test details; the current amended text applies.

related.title: Face shields / visors for protective helmets
related.relation: Referenced for the optical and mechanical performance of the visor.

certification.summary: Two-wheeler helmets are under compulsory BIS certification. A manufacturer must hold a Scheme I licence and put the ISI mark with the CM/L number on every helmet. Manufacture, import, storage for sale or sale of a helmet without the ISI mark is prohibited.

applicable.name: Scheme I (ISI Mark Scheme)
applicable.covers: Licence to use the ISI mark on protective helmets after factory assessment and testing of samples against IS 4151.
applicable.why: The QCO issued by MoRTH places helmets under mandatory ISI-mark certification with a factory Scheme of Inspection and Testing.
applicable.you_receive: A BIS licence with a CM/L number and the right to mark each helmet with the ISI mark; normally valid for 2 years and renewable.

not_applicable.name: Scheme II (CRS)
not_applicable.why: CRS is only for electronics and IT goods notified by MeitY. Helmets are safety equipment under Scheme I.

not_applicable.name: Scheme X
not_applicable.why: Scheme X is for machinery/equipment to a purchaser's specification, not for a mass-market safety helmet.

testing.summary: Sample helmets drawn from the factory are tested at a BIS / BIS-recognised laboratory against IS 4151. The factory also conducts routine and acceptance tests under its SIT.

tests.name: Shock absorption (impact) test at specified points and temperatures
Retention system strength and effectiveness (roll-off) test
Mass of helmet within specified limit
Visor luminous transmittance and mechanical strength
Conditioning: ambient, high temperature, low temperature, water immersion, solar radiation before impact

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual for IS 4151 - tests and SIT

labs.note: Helmet testing needs a laboratory with IS 4151 in its recognised scope and a helmet impact rig. Confirm scope and validity in the BIS LIMS directory before dispatching samples.

entries.name: Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET)

licensing.summary: Scheme I (ISI mark) licence for helmets is applied for online on Manak Online: apply and pay -> scrutiny -> factory inspection and sample drawal -> testing against IS 4151 -> grant of licence with CM/L number.

steps.title: Apply online on Manak Online
steps.detail: Register the firm, file the Scheme I application for IS 4151, upload documents, declare the SIT and in-house test facility, and pay the fee.

steps.title: Scrutiny of application
steps.detail: BIS checks the manufacturing capability, machinery and test facility and raises queries.
steps.timeline: About 15-30 days after a complete application

steps.title: Factory inspection and sample drawal
steps.detail: A BIS officer inspects the unit, witnesses in-house tests and seals samples for independent testing.

steps.title: Independent testing against IS 4151
steps.detail: Samples tested at a BIS / recognised lab; conditioning plus impact, penetration, retention, rigidity, vision and mass checks.
steps.timeline: Several weeks depending on lab queue

steps.title: Grant of licence
steps.detail: On a satisfactory report, BIS grants the licence and CM/L number; helmets may then be ISI-marked. Licence normally valid 2 years, renewable.
steps.timeline: Commonly around 4 months from a clean application

documents.summary: Documents for the Scheme I helmet application. Conditional items depend on the firm's constitution, brand and whether the applicant is an importer.

items.name: Firm / factory establishment proof
items.explanation: Business registration, GST, factory licence or Udyam registration, and factory address proof.

items.name: Manufacturing process flow chart and machinery list
items.explanation: Shows shell moulding, EPS liner forming, assembly and finishing are done in-house.

items.name: List of test equipment with calibration certificates
items.explanation: In-house facility for routine checks (mass, dimensions, retention, visor transmittance).

sources.doc: BIS Product Manual for IS 4151 - SIT

items.name: Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT)
items.explanation: Documented raw-material, in-process, routine and acceptance test plan with records.

items.name: Product test report against IS 4151 (if available)
items.explanation: Supports the application; independent BIS testing is still carried out.

items.name: Authorised signatory authorisation and ID
items.explanation: Board resolution / partnership authorisation plus ID of the signatory.

items.name: Trademark / brand ownership proof
items.explanation: If the helmet carries a registered brand owned or licensed by the applicant.

items.name: Importer: Authorised Indian Representative (AIR) papers
items.explanation: Foreign manufacturers apply through an AIR with the appointment letter and undertakings.
